title: HTTP Status Codes Usage
summary: Proper HTTP status codes inform clients about the result of their requests, distinguishing success, client error, and server error.

content.overview: Using standard HTTP status codes correctly is crucial for API clarity and client error handling.
content.details: Common codes: 200 OK successful request; 201 Created resource created; 400 Bad Request invalid input; 401 Unauthorized authentication required; 403 Forbidden authenticated but not authorized; 404 Not Found resource missing; 500 Internal Server Error server-side error.
content.examples: Returning 201 Created with Location header after resource creation; returning 400 Bad Request with validation error details.
content.caveats: Avoid using 200 for everything; choose the most specific status code for the situation.
